Quirenote · design extension · brief #496 · implementing #494, then #317

Re-authentication: «Підтвердьте, що це ви» after a sensitive action’s confirmation

The step that follows S4’s «Продовжити» on /profile, before #494 ends every session the account holds, and before #317 deletes the account, which brings its own lines. The same dialog swaps its content to the step; a passkey or the password proves it, or a round trip to Google for an account with no password. Brief: #496, a comment on the issue.

T1 · The confirmation and the first state

One dialog, top-anchored. S4’s confirmation stands where the step will: 64 from the top at ≥ md and 16 below, 420 wide and 100vw − 32 below, so «Продовжити» swaps the content without the edge moving, and every step grows downward from it. WHATWG’s dialog editor: «Having the dialog move up and down when stuff is added at the bottom would be quite weird»; Bootstrap top-anchors by default, Atlassian’s positioner keeps a «60px base gutter», Primer’s align="top" stands «~4rem from the top». Below md the row stacks full width with the action above «Скасувати», Material’s «Affirmative actions are stacked above dismissive actions», since the step’s pairs pass 270 side by side; the action comes first in the DOM there too, so the focus order is the drawn order (WCAG 2.4.3). An AlertDialog: an outside click never closes it. Escape closes it at any moment but while the action is in flight, when «Скасувати» is busy too; «Скасувати» stays pressable while a proof is checked (a late answer lands nowhere, as sign-in’s does) and goes busy only once the action is sent or the page leaves for Google, since a sent sign-out cannot be recalled (GOV.UK: «Disabled buttons have poor contrast and can confuse some users, so avoid them if possible»). The type is the dialog’s own, S4’s: the title at 18 / 24, the lead at 12 / 18 muted, so the flow reads as one dialog; the field, the check, the sentences and the link are sign-in’s. Its height is capped at the visible viewport less the keyboard, less its top offset above and below: (100dvh − --keyboard-inset) − 128 at ≥ md and − 32 below, where Dialog.tsx caps a centred panel at 85 % of 100dvh − --keyboard-inset and lifts it by half the inset; top-anchored, the lift has nothing to do, so a focused password field stays above the keyboard, and past the cap the whole panel scrolls inside its edge, title, body, row and the lines under it, through one Scroller, so a sentence or the retry’s check under the row stays reachable on a short landscape view (Bootstrap’s default: «When modals become too long for the user’s viewport or device, they scroll independent of the page itself»; its body-only scroll is the opt-in). The mechanism is #494’s. The tallest panel drawn ends at 432,5 of 900 and 442,5 of 740 with no keyboard (T7).

The first state asks the way sign-in does, identifier-first: the address is shown, not typed, and «Підтвердити» sends it with a fresh check; the answer opens the passkey sheet when the account holds a passkey and leads to the password otherwise (T2, T3). Its heading takes focus; no sheet opens before the press. An account with no passkey and no password gets «Продовжити з Google» in the action’s place and no check, since /auth/google/begin is not /auth/start. While registration is closed every account holds a password, so this is the state opening registration brings (Auth model).

T2 · The passkey

The OS sheet is the action, so the row holds «Скасувати» and the account’s second way, an outline or Google’s own button: «Підтвердити паролем» when the account has a password, else «Продовжити з Google» when Google is linked, else nothing beside «Скасувати», the retry and the OS sheet’s own other-device option remaining (passkeys.dev: other methods «assuming the user has such other sign in methods available to them»; WebAuthn’s hybrid transport). Every account holds a password while registration is closed, so the last two are the states opening registration brings. Cancelled or answered with no passkey, reauth.passkey.notFinished, the confirmation’s own wording of sign-in’s sentence, stands 12 under the row, the retry’s check 12 under it and «Спробувати ще раз» 16 under the check, the gap its 44 × 44 hit area is owed (tap-target.ts), as bot-check-steps.dc.html places them on sign-in. Answered, the lead turns to a status held in its own line, «Перевіряємо…», «Підтвердити паролем» busy and «Скасувати» live; verified, the action runs at once, «Виходимо…» in the same line and every control busy: RFC 9470’s client «repeats the request», and OWASP’s transaction authorization runs confirm, then credentials, then «validates authorization and executes». This device then signs out and lands as sign-out-landing.dc.html draws it.

T3 · The password, and what it answers

The field and its reserved line, then the check, then the row: sign-in’s password step in the dialog’s gutter. The field takes focus. A refusal is one sentence 12 under the row and the typed password stays; the field’s edge never turns neg, as on sign-in. A wrong password names the password alone, «Неправильний пароль.»: the address is the signed-in account’s own, so the generic sentence that guards account existence for an unknown caller guards nothing here. Too many attempts is the shipped sentence, with no counter of the app’s own (NIST SP 800-63B-4 counts per authenticator). Pressed empty, the step refuses on the field’s own reserved line, «Вкажіть пароль.», the edge in neg and the field aria-invalid, and sends nothing, as sign-in’s does. Verified, «Підтвердити» reads «Виходимо…» and the action runs at once.

T4 · The bot check

The first state and the password step each carry the slot every /auth/start takes (Auth model), between the content and the row, at 65. At 360 the widget keeps its 300 minimum, centred, 15 past each side of the panel’s 270 content box (326 inside its border, less the two 28 gutters) and 14 inside the panel’s outer edge (Cloudflare: «Flexible 100% (min: 300px)»). Failed or unloaded, the shipped sentences stand 12 under the row. Pressed before its token, the first state refuses with «Перевірка безпеки ще триває. Спробуйте ще раз за мить.» and sends nothing, since its start opens the passkey sheet; the password step’s press waits for the token, busy, and sends it then, as sign-in’s does.

T5 · Google: leaving, the return, the time left

«Продовжити з Google» goes busy and the page leaves. On /auth/callback the card account-way-in-and-out.dc.html T5 draws holds «Перевіряємо…» and «Завершуємо підтвердження через Google.». Back on /profile the dialog opens on the confirmed state: its heading focused, the lead, the time left, «Скасувати» and the filled «Вийти всюди»; nothing runs without the press (Auth0 added one after scanners ran an on-load action; NIST SP 800-63B-4: a live Google session can pass «without explicitly reauthenticating»).

The time left is «Залишилося 5 хв» in whole minutes rounded up, redrawn once a minute, then seconds from 60 on, «Залишилося 40 с», so «1 хв» never shows: hmrc-frontend’s timeout dialog switches at roundedRemaining <= 60000, through Intl.DurationFormat short. At the lead’s 12 / 18, so it never outranks the lead. A silent role="timer" (WAI-ARIA: «implicit aria-live value of off»), read once with the step’s description, then one polite reminder at a minute. No extend control: WCAG 2.2.1’s essential exception covers security limits «such as time-based / time-limited two-factor authentication tokens», and confirming again is the extension. It shows wherever the window can run out: here, and after an action that failed and waits for its retry, whichever proof came before it, so a passkey or password that succeeded lands on this state too when the action fails. Refused or abandoned at Google, the first state returns with «Підтвердження через Google не завершено.».

T6 · The window runs out

At zero, or on a press the server refuses as too old, the step returns to its first state with «Час на підтвердження минув. Підтвердьте ще раз.» under its row, as bot-check-steps.dc.html T4 returns an expired set-password; nothing redirects by itself. The sentence is a role="status", the state of the application (WCAG 4.1.3, ARIA22); focus moves to it when it was in the step, and at zero no focused button’s label changes under it.

T10 · Refused, and not drawn

  • Refused: a second dialog over the confirmation; a page of its own; a centred panel that grows both ways; a second press between a passkey or password that succeeded in the dialog and the action (a failed action lands on the confirmed state, T5); a height transition on the panel; the action running on the return from Google; Google offered beside a password, or a «Підтвердити паролем» for an account that has none; the session’s own method; an emailed code; an extend control; «4:59» or a clock time; a timer announced each tick or each minute; the sentence at zero as an alert; a redirect at zero; a toast for a refusal (NN/g: «Display the error message close to the error’s source»).
  • Not drawn: the check’s passed and checkbox looks outside the busy states, which bot-check.dc.html draws; the signed-out landing after the action, which sign-out-landing.dc.html draws; the English frames, whose strings T9 carries; deletion’s own lines (#317).
  • Handed to #494 as requirements, not drawn: how the app knows an account has no local credential (GET /me gains the flag when registration opens); how the confirmed state survives the redirect, held by this tab alone and never run from the URL; where the timer’s 5 minutes start, the token’s own auth_time; every status line, the passkey’s, the expired one and the timer’s one reminder, a region in place before its words, as SignedOutNote’s is (parts.tsx); focus kept in the dialog when the pressed button goes busy, where sign-in’s disabled drops it to the page (SignIn.tsx); Escape ignored while the action is in flight (Radix onEscapeKeyDown); the dev reading of auth_time after a refresh and after a Google round trip.
